sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul J. 2000. Proto South Bahnaric: a reconstruction of a Mon-Khmer language of Indo-China. Pacific Linguistics 501. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Genus-level only (p. 40): minor syllables 'are always unstressed, and can be dropped in speech if it does not cause ambiguity' -- said of South Bahnaric (Chrau, Stieng, Koho, Mnong) generally; Kraol is never named in the book (0 hits).

sources.citation: Butler, Becky A. 2014. Deconstructing the Southeast Asian Sesquisyllable: A Gestural Account. PhD dissertation, Cornell University.
sources.note: Kraol mentioned once (p. 101) in a list of South Bahnaric languages; phonetic study is of Central Bunong only; nothing on Kraol stress.

sources.citation: Barr & Pawley 2013 live copy, SIL ESR 2013-001 (sil.org entry 52517)
sources.note: Already downloaded via the Internet Archive and read in full: silent on stress. Listed only so the compilers records that the scan's 'unreachable' source has now been opened.

sources.citation: Barr, Julie & Eric Pawley. 2013. Bahnaric Language Cluster Survey of Mondul Kiri and Kratie Provinces, Cambodia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-001. 132 pp. (downloaded via the Internet Archive; live sil.org copy is behind an automated-access block)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey: Kraol section 4.2.1 (villages, vitality), Kraol IPA wordlists (varieties V14 Roya, V30 Ampok, V31 Srae Chis; App. I, txt pp. ~101ff), Appendices F/G on presyllables/sesquisyllabic words (Bunong-focused). No use of 'stress', 'prominence', 'tone' in a phonological sense; 'accent' occurs only re. a Khmer accent. Wordlist transcriptions show reduced superscript-schwa presyllables (e.g. sᵊmaɲ 'star', tʰᵊmoː 'stone') but no stress marks and no prose statement.

sources.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Jennifer Herington & Paul Sidwell. 2013. Bahnaric linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-xlvii.
sources.note: Bibliography check only: the sole Kraol-related item is 'International Cooperation Cambodia (ICC). 2006. Bahnaric Language Cluster Survey' (= the survey later published as Barr & Pawley 2013). No Kraol phonology/grammar listed as of 2013.

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A Survey of Word Accentual Patterns in the Languages of the World, 509-613. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: Kraol appears only in the Mon-Khmer classification tree (under Mnong: Southern-Central). Family-level generalization: Mon-Khmer sesquisyllabic words have 'the iambic rhythm of an unaccented presyllable and an accented main syllable'; Bahnaric exemplified by Chrau (Thomas 1971:31). No Kraol data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page krao1238; Wikipedia 'Kraol language' (redirects to Mnong language)
sources.note: Nothing on Kraol prosody; Glottolog treats Kraol as a Southern-Central Mnong variety; no grammar/phonology reference listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2021. Bahnaric (classification / overview chapters). In Paul Sidwell & Mathias Jenny (eds.), The Languages and Linguistics of Mainland Southeast Asia: A Comprehensive Guide. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.citation: Butler, Becky. 2015. Bunong. In Mathias Jenny & Paul Sidwell (eds.), The Handbook of Austroasiatic Languages, vol. 1, 719-745. Leiden: Brill.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Closest described variety: Glottolog files Kraol under Southern-Central Mnong together with Central Mnong (Bunong); the Handbook sketch has a word/syllable-structure and phonology section that would supply the nearest first-hand stress statement if Kraol is catalogued as a Mnong dialect.
